title: Burden-weighted epilepsy TARGET prioritisation (cited tiers + declared weights)
principle: ranks READS/TARGETS, not drugs. B/U/G are CITED tiers; the weights are a declared editorial choice -> the ranking is [F] from tiers+weights, NOT a [V] engine output. gamma-|h_sp| is carried ALONGSIDE as structural context and is NEVER folded into the score (firewall: a promoter-stiffness read is not a clinical magnitude). efficacy=0; no molecule, dose, or patient is ranked.

decoupling_witness.reading: the stiffest promoter read (CACNA1H) sits LOW on priority while the top-priority burden gene (SCN1A) has one of the SOFTEST reads -- if promoter stiffness drove the ranking neither could sit where it does. The decoupling is the firewall made visible.

ranking.cite: Dravet syndrome, high SUDEP; the most-replicated monogenic epilepsy gene (Claes 2001) -- but the L1 Na-block direction is CONTRAINDICATED in Dravet
KCNQ2 encephalopathy + benign familial neonatal epilepsy; the M-current brake with the clearest mechanism and the retigabine K_V7-opener precedent (Weckhuysen 2012)

ranking.channel_or_protein: tuberin (TSC2; mTORC1 repressor complex, GAP for Rheb)
ranking.cite: tuberous sclerosis (severe, often drug-resistant epilepsy); tuberin is the Rheb-GAP; everolimus is an approved mTOR-inhibition DIRECTION (French 2016)
malignant migrating partial seizures of infancy (EIMFS), extremely drug-resistant; quinidine is a KCNT1-GOF channel-block DIRECTION (Barcia 2012; Bearden 2014)
leading cause of familial focal epilepsy incl. focal cortical dysplasia; GATOR1/mTOR repressor -> mTOR-inhibition precision DIRECTION (Dibbens 2013)
tuberous sclerosis (hamartin); mTOR-inhibition DIRECTION (van Slegtenhorst 1997; French 2016)
SCN2A gain-of-function early-infantile epileptic encephalopathy, Na-blocker responsive (Wolff 2017); shared neuropsychiatric Na gene
SCN8A gain-of-function epileptic encephalopathy (EIEE13); persistent-Na+ GOF is the Na-blocker-responsive case (Veeramah 2012)
GRIN2A epilepsy-aphasia spectrum (Landau-Kleffner/CSWS); glutamatergic NMDA DIRECTION (Lemke 2013; Lesca 2013)
KCNB1 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; the major somatic delayed-rectifier brake (Torkamani 2014)
GABA-A alpha1 in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy and DEE; the inhibitory GABAergic restoring current (Cossette 2002)
GABA-A gamma2 in GEFS+/febrile seizures; the benzodiazepine-site inhibitory brake (Baulac 2001; Wallace 2001)
KCNQ3 benign familial neonatal epilepsy; M-current partner of K_V7.2 (Charlier 1998)
P/Q-type Ca-channel in absence epilepsy + episodic-ataxia overlap (Jouvenceau 2001)
T-type Ca_V3.2 in childhood absence epilepsy; ethosuximide T-type DIRECTION is established/low unmet (Chen 2003) -- note: STIFFEST promoter read yet LOW priority (decoupling)
K_V1.1 episodic ataxia type 1 with epilepsy; rarer, weaker direct pharmacological handle (Browne 1994)
